about.title: 认识佛寿寺
about.intro: 佛寿寺位于费城樱桃街，是一处礼佛共修的道场。
about.body: 佛寿寺由释贤参法师住持。寺院每天上午八点十五分至下午五点半开放，欢迎来寺礼佛、上香。寺院主要举办法会和诵经共修，也有佛前大供和下午晚课。
about.practiceText: 寺院每周日举行共修，诵经以普通话为主。佛菩萨圣诞法会通常在农历正日举行，实际日期和时间以寺院公告为准。
about.welcomeText: 来寺礼佛或参加共修都无需登记。每次共修后，楼下都有免费素斋。
about.galleryIntro: 大殿、地藏殿和往生堂都是寺院日常礼佛、诵经和供养的场所。

home.title: A place to practice together
home.intro: Visit Fo Shou Temple in Philadelphia to pay respects to the Buddha and offer incense. We’re open daily from 8:15 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. No registration is needed.
home.weeklyIntro: We chant mainly in Mandarin. You’re welcome to join without registering.
home.calendarIntro: Explore major Buddhist commemorations and the birthdays of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. Related Dharma assemblies are usually held on the lunar anniversary; temple announcements confirm each assembly.
home.aboutText: Fo Shou Temple in Philadelphia is led by Venerable Shi Xian Can (釋賢參法師). We gather for Buddhist worship, chanting, and offerings before the Buddha, welcoming both first-time visitors and those returning to practice with us.
home.offeringsText: A free vegetarian meal is served downstairs after each communal practice gathering. Everyone is welcome to eat. You are also welcome to make offerings for the meals in person and cultivate merit through generosity.

about.title: Our Temple
about.intro: A place for Buddhist worship and communal practice on Cherry Street in Philadelphia.
about.body: Fo Shou Temple is led by Venerable Shi Xian Can (釋賢參法師). The temple is open daily from 8:15 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. for visitors to pay respects to the Buddha and offer incense. Temple gatherings include chanting, offerings before the Buddha, a free vegetarian meal after communal practice, and afternoon liturgy.
about.practiceText: Communal practice takes place every Sunday, primarily in Mandarin Chinese. Dharma assemblies marking the birthdays of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are usually held on the lunar anniversary. Please see temple announcements for dates and times.
about.welcomeText: No registration is required. You are welcome to visit during daily opening hours or join a communal practice gathering. A free vegetarian meal is provided downstairs after each gathering.
about.galleryIntro: The Buddha hall, Ksitigarbha Hall, and Rebirth Hall are spaces for daily worship, chanting, and offerings at Fo Shou Temple.

services.title: Dharma Assemblies & Practice
services.intro: We gather for chanting on Sundays and hold Dharma assemblies on the first and fifteenth days of each lunar month.
services.mealText: Everyone is welcome to share a meal downstairs.
services.afternoonText: Chanting usually ends between 2 and 3 p.m.
services.specialText: Our calendar includes major Buddhist observances. Dharma assemblies are usually held on the lunar anniversary. Please check temple announcements for specific times and arrangements.
services.noticeText: Check temple announcements for special Dharma assemblies or changes to the regular schedule.
services.eventAttendance: Practice is mainly in Mandarin, and you’re welcome to attend without registering.
services.afterPracticeMeal: After practice, join us downstairs for a free vegetarian meal.

offerings.title: Offerings & Vegetarian Meals
offerings.intro: You’re welcome to join us for offerings before the Buddha and share a vegetarian meal after practice.
offerings.offeringText: Offerings before the Buddha are part of our communal practice, alongside chanting and worship. The regular Sunday morning gathering runs from 10 to 11:30 a.m.
offerings.mealTitle: A free vegetarian meal after practice
offerings.mealText: A free vegetarian meal is served downstairs after each communal practice gathering. Everyone is welcome to eat. On Sundays, the meal follows morning practice.
offerings.invitation: Everyone is welcome to make offerings for the temple’s vegetarian meals in person and cultivate merit through generosity.

visit.title: Visit & Contact
visit.intro: Come to pay respects to the Buddha, offer incense, or join us for practice.
visit.languageText: Communal practice is conducted primarily in Mandarin Chinese.
visit.hoursNote: You’re welcome to drop in during these hours. No registration is needed.
visit.firstVisitText: See the Sunday schedule if you’d like to practice with us. Dates and times for special Dharma assemblies appear in temple announcements.

faq.q: What language is used during practice?
faq.a: Communal practice is conducted primarily in Mandarin Chinese.

faq.q: Can I share a meal at the temple?
faq.a: Yes. A free vegetarian meal is provided downstairs after each communal practice gathering. On Sundays, it follows morning practice.
